business_problem: SNCF Connect needed to replace an Oracle database that had become difficult to scale and maintain as ticket sales and connection volumes surged across its national rail-booking application.
solution_summary: SNCF Connect & Tech migrated the data layer behind its high-volume ticketing app from Oracle to MongoDB Atlas so it could support growth, seasonal surges, and new passenger-facing features. A multidisciplinary team designed the target platform around RTO, RPO, purging, and continuous-backup requirements, then built an asynchronous migration process that transferred 130 million orders into Atlas while an observability tool and throttling mechanisms protected service quality. The cutover was staged across four phases with repeated performance, API, batch, and scalability testing. Once on Atlas, SNCF implemented technical and business indexes for operational and customer-support searches, applied a TTL index to automate order purging, and used Atlas Functions to process deletion events. A rollback mapping between Oracle and MongoDB identifiers let the application safely read from either source during parallel runs, reducing migration risk while the new platform became the primary system.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores orders for the SNCF Connect application and provides the managed multi-stage migration target that replaced Oracle.

solution_components.name: Atlas Function
solution_components.role: Processes delete events for purged orders after TTL expiration so related entries can be handled automatically.

data_flow: Order data is migrated asynchronously from Oracle into MongoDB Atlas, indexed for customer and support searches, purged automatically through TTL rules, and passed to Atlas Functions when deletion events need follow-on handling.
business_outcome: SNCF Connect completed a low-disruption migration, scaled ticketing workloads for major seasonal spikes, and gave the app a more maintainable search- and purge-ready operational database.
metrics: More than 550,000 tickets are sold through the app every day.
In 2023, the database behind SNCF Connect was processing 1 million connections per minute, up from 300,000 the year before.
The team transferred 130 million orders; the full data transfer took 18.5 hours and the final delta transfer took 30 minutes.
architecture_clues: The migration was executed in four stages with performance, API reliability, batch processing, and scalability tests at every stage.
Indexes are split into technical and business categories for search and support workflows.
A TTL index on lastModifiedDate automates order purging.
A rollback collection maps Oracle and MongoDB identifiers down to sub-document level.
evidence_quotes: “Adopting MongoDB Atlas for this project was a no brainer — it has the right document model and with our in-house expertise, we were confident we could migrate from Oracle to MongoDB Atlas with minimal disruption to customers.”
The team developed an asynchronous process to transfer 130 million orders from the legacy database into MongoDB.
“Our tests confirmed that MongoDB Atlas was the right choice — it couldn’t be faulted.”
“Thanks to the commitment and expertise of all teams involved, the migration was a resounding success. The project was seamless and there was minimal disruption to SNCF Connect users.”
